title: Sequential Crews: Pipelines of Agents
objective: After this lesson you will be able to run sequential agent crews with stage contracts, replay any stage from logged handoffs, and decide when sequential suffices versus hierarchical routing.
why: Not every team needs a manager: catalog pipelines (research → write → review), triage flows, and audit chains run fixed order with full determinism of structure. Sequential crews are the multi-agent default — cheaper, traceable, replayable — and the baseline every fancier topology must beat. Start here; escalate to hierarchy on measured need, never ambition.

blocks.text: A **sequential crew** runs tasks in declared order, each consuming the prior handoff: research output feeds writer, writer output feeds reviewer. Every stage holds its Ch.3 contract, so the pipeline is verifiable joint-by-joint. Real CrewAI: `Crew(agents=[...], tasks=[...], process=Process.sequential)` — tasks execute in list order with outputs passed as context.

blocks.caption: Gated stages in order; failures name stages with evidence

blocks.text: Logged handoffs make every stage re-runnable in isolation: replay reviewer with writer's logged output (no re-running research), test writer variants against frozen inputs, bisect failures to stages. Replayability is sequential crews' superpower over tangled graphs — structure simplicity pays in debuggability.

blocks.caption: Logged handoffs are time machines for stages

blocks.text: Escalate to hierarchical when: steps need **skipping** by judgment (fraud check only sometimes), **ordering** varies per case, or **parallel** branches must join. Symptoms in a sequential crew: conditional hacks inside stages ('if VIP skip'), growing context dumps 'just in case', re-runs of whole pipelines for one stage's fix. Each symptom names the missing dynamicism — escalate on evidence, Ch.5 builds the pattern.

blocks.title: Run the pipeline
blocks.note: Run it: expect ok=true, stages research,write,review, and the draft carrying the facts forward. Then delete 'facts' from research's return and re-run: failure names stage 'write' with the log proving research's shortfall.

items: Sequential crews: fixed order, contracted stages, gated handoffs — the multi-agent default
Logged handoffs enable stage replay: isolate variants, bisect failures, freeze inputs
Escalate on evidence (skips, ordering variance, parallelism) — symptoms name the missing dynamicism

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice pipeline and record the draft. (b) Break research's output (drop facts) and record the failure shape. (c) Replay review with a frozen writer output and a variant reviewer (strict vs lenient) — state what replay proves that re-running cannot.
hints: Baseline: ok=true, three stages, draft references facts. Breakage: ok=false, failedAt write, log shows research's empty handoff.
Replay: carry = logged writer output, run variant reviewers only — upstream untouched, variant effects isolated.
Replay proves stage-local causality (reviewer differences with identical inputs); re-running confounds stage noise with input noise.
exercise.why: Failure naming (stage + evidence) plus replay causality are sequential crews' debugging superpowers — practiced on breakage, not just success paths.
exercise.code: // Break-and-replay pattern: mutate one stage, read failure shape, replay variants.

options: Sequential crew: fixed pipeline, no dynamicism needed — cheaper, traceable, replayable
quiz.explain: Fixed order with contracted stages is sequential's home turf. Fancier topologies add cost without function.

quiz.q: Writer variant test without re-running research. Mechanism?
options: Replay from logged handoffs: frozen writer inputs, variant reviewer — upstream untouched
quiz.explain: Logged handoffs are time machines: isolate stage variants on frozen inputs for causal proof.

quiz.q: Stages sprout 'if VIP skip' hacks. Meaning?
options: Escalation symptom: conditional flow needs hierarchical routing — hacks signal missing dynamicism
quiz.explain: Conditionals inside fixed stages fight the topology. Symptoms prescribe: skip/order variance → hierarchical (Ch.5).

summary: Sequential crews run contracted stages in fixed order with gated handoffs and full replay. Default choice; escalate on measured dynamicism.
next: Fixed flows handled — now judgment calls: manager delegation, budgets, and termination proofs. Next: hierarchical crews.
